question: According to the sign convention, the height of an erect image formed by a mirror is taken as:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Positive**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sign Convention in Optics:** In the study of mirrors, the **height of an erect image** is taken as **positive** according to the sign convention.
 
• **Image Formation:** An erect image is formed when the image is upright relative to the object. Such images are formed by **plane mirrors** or certain configurations of concave and convex mirrors.
 
• **Positive Height:** The sign convention defines erect images as positive because they lie above the principal axis in diagrams. This is an essential aspect of ray diagrams in geometrical optics.
 
• **Nature of Erect Images:** Erect images are typically **virtual images**, meaning the light rays do not actually converge at the image location but appear to do so.
 
• The correct answer is **Positive**, as per standard optical sign conventions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Sign Convention in Optics:**

 
 
• The sign convention used in optics is derived from **Cartesian coordinate system**.
 
• Distances measured in the direction of incident light are considered **positive**, while those measured against it are considered **negative**.
 
• Similarly, heights of images above the principal axis are positive, and those below are negative.
 
 
 
• **Real vs Virtual Images:**
 
 
• **Real images** are formed when light rays converge at a point. These images are inverted, and their height is negative as per the convention.
 
• **Virtual images**, on the other hand, are formed when light rays appear to diverge from a point. These images are erect, and their height is positive.
 
 
 
• **Examples of Erect Images:**
 
 
• A virtual image formed by a **plane mirror** is erect and has a positive height.
 
• Convex mirrors also form erect virtual images.
 
• Concave mirrors can form erect images when the object is placed within the focal length.
 
 
 
• **Applications:**
 
 
• **Rearview mirrors** in vehicles use convex mirrors to produce erect and diminished images of objects behind the vehicle.
 
• Plane mirrors are used in **daily life** for grooming and decoration because they produce erect images.
 
• Optical instruments such as **telescopes** and **microscopes** often utilize mirrors and lenses to manipulate image orientation.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Plane Mirror:** Always forms virtual, erect, and same-sized images.
 
• **Convex Mirror:** Forms virtual, erect, and diminished images irrespective of the object's distance.
 
• **Concave Mirror:** Forms erect virtual images when the object is placed between the focal point and the mirror.
 
• **Key Concept in Physics:** Sign conventions are critical in solving numerical problems in ray optics, such as determining focal lengths, image distances, and magnifications.
